earth.name: Earth Surface (1.0 g)
earth.description: Standard terrestrial gravity. Strong buoyancy forces generate natural convection, causing hot gases to rise rapidly and pulling ambient air inward at the flame base.

mars.name: Mars Gravity (0.38 g)
mars.description: Reduced Martian gravitational acceleration (simulated in experimental habitat). Buoyant upward velocity is reduced by ~38%, resulting in wider flame geometry and lower convective cooling.

moon.name: Lunar Gravity (0.165 g)
moon.description: Lunar habitat gravity (~1/6th Earth). Buoyancy is sluggish; molecular diffusion begins to govern species transport away from the reaction zone.

microgravity.name: Orbital Microgravity (~10⁻⁴ g)
microgravity.description: Orbiting spacecraft / ISS environment. Buoyant convection vanishes; combustion forms a quiet spherical diffusion flame dependent purely on molecular diffusion or forced spacecraft ventilation.

artemis_cabin.name: Exploration Atmosphere (34% O₂ @ 56 kPa)
artemis_cabin.description: NASA Exploration Atmosphere for next-generation Artemis spacecraft (reduced pressure, elevated oxygen to minimize EVA pre-breathe time while testing flammability margins).
